security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md and reference findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples and genomics option names. The confirmed risks are in scripts/workflow_generator.py, which writes shell scripts with unescaped user-provided paths and writes to caller-selected output files. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Generated bash templates embed user-controlled paths without shell escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Escape every generated shell value with shlex.quote or pass arguments through arrays with strict quoting in the generated script.

remediation.issue: The workflow generator writes to arbitrary output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output files to the working directory, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and warn before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Generated scripts are presented as runnable immediately after creation.
remediation.suggestion: Add a review step that tells users to inspect paths, commands, and output directories before chmod or execution.

content.value_statement: NGS analysis often requires careful command selection, normalization, and file validation. This skill helps users build deepTools workflows for coverage, QC, comparison, and visualization.
actual_capabilities: Explains deepTools commands for BAM, bigWig, BED, and matrix-based analyses.
Generates workflow templates for ChIP-seq QC, ChIP-seq analysis, RNA-seq coverage, and ATAC-seq analysis.
Guides normalization choices such as RPGC, CPM, RPKM, BPM, and read count scaling.
Provides file validation guidance for BAM indexes, bigWig files, and BED region files.
Builds command sequences for correlation plots, PCA, fingerprints, heatmaps, and profile plots.
References effective genome sizes for common organisms used in RPGC normalization.
limitations: It depends on deepTools and related command-line tools being installed locally.
Generated workflow scripts require user review before execution on real data.
It does not validate biological study design or replace expert genomics review.
Large datasets may need cluster resources or manual performance tuning.

use_cases.title: Prepare ChIP-seq QC
use_cases.description: Create a quality control workflow with correlation, PCA, coverage, fragment size, and fingerprint outputs.

use_cases.title: Build Coverage Tracks
use_cases.description: Choose normalization settings and convert aligned BAM files into genome browser ready bigWig tracks.

use_cases.title: Visualize Regulatory Signal
use_cases.description: Design computeMatrix, plotHeatmap, and plotProfile steps around genes, peaks, or other genomic regions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a QC Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user with aligned ChIP-seq BAM files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a deepTools ChIP-seq QC workflow for one input BAM and two ChIP BAM files. Explain each output.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Normalization
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs coverage tracks for comparison.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have BAM files from the same genome build. Recommend a deepTools normalization method for comparing signal across samples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Heatmap Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: User has signal tracks and genomic regions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a computeMatrix and plotHeatmap workflow around TSS regions using my bigWig files and gene BED file.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Full Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants validation before execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned deepTools workflow for ATAC-seq. Check Tn5 correction, normalization, fragment analysis, and heatmap steps.

output_examples.input: I need to compare treatment and control ChIP-seq BAM files.
output_examples.output: A recommended bamCompare workflow with log2 ratio output, read count scaling, duplicate handling, and follow-up heatmap guidance.

output_examples.input: My BAM files are ready, but I do not know which QC plots to run.
output_examples.output: A QC plan covering sample correlation, PCA, coverage distribution, fragment size checks, and ChIP enrichment fingerprints.

output_examples.input: I want strand-specific RNA-seq coverage tracks.
output_examples.output: A coverage plan using bamCoverage with strand filtering, CPM normalization, and a warning not to extend RNA-seq reads.

best_practices: Validate BAM indexes, BED format, and file readability before running deepTools commands.
Choose normalization based on the experiment type and comparison goal.
Test commands on small genomic regions before processing full datasets.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated shell scripts without reviewing file paths and output directories.
Do not mix genome assemblies between BAM files, BED files, and effective genome size values.
Do not use ChIP-seq read extension settings for RNA-seq coverage analysis.

faq.question: What experiments does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports deepTools workflows for ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, and related NGS signal analysis.

faq.question: Can it generate runnable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a workflow generator, but users should review generated shell scripts before execution.

faq.question: Does it install deepTools?
faq.answer: It provides installation guidance, but the user environment must have deepTools and required dependencies available.

faq.question: Can it validate my files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included validation script checks file existence, BAM indexes, bigWig size, and basic BED formatting.

faq.question: Which normalization method should I use?
faq.answer: The skill explains RPGC, CPM, RPKM, BPM, and read count scaling based on the experiment and comparison goal.

faq.question: Is it safe for automated execution?
faq.answer: Generated workflows should not be run automatically with untrusted paths because shell escaping is not enforced.
